evidence.scope: pre-pilot main research sources as of Nov 11 2026

results.title: Should we prioritize AI grant vetting?
results.claim: AI grant vetting is the most attractive first DAF technology differentiation
results.conclusion: Test donor engagement and end-to-end workflow exceptions before committing to standalone AI grant vetting.

frameworkUse.reason: observable survey outcomes; causal origins remain hypothetical

results.counterargument: Self-rated grant review effectiveness could coexist with high handling cost, errors, and unmet buyer demand.
results.action: Conduct consented sponsor buyer discovery and cost/exception measurement; compare grant vetting with donor engagement.
monitor: manual exception cost per completed grant
results.reassessWhen: Current buyer interviews or independent measurements find larger validated grant-vetting costs or willingness-to-pay than engagement workflow.

results.title: Are 3.59 million DAF accounts the software TAM?
results.claim: DAFRC's FY2024 3.59 million DAF accounts represent distinct paying enterprise DAF platform customers
results.conclusion: The national account total cannot be used directly to calculate enterprise platform TAM; segment processor accounts and verify paid vendor contracts.

frameworkUse.reason: known report aggregation and classification heterogeneity

results.counterargument: Donation processors can still pay software vendors; classify buyers rather than excluding a segment categorically.
results.action: Download revised sponsor-level DAFRC data and map sponsoring entities to actual vendor contract types.
results.reassessWhen: A versioned sponsor-year dataset and comparable contractual vendor/customer monetization allow an audited serviceable-market estimate.

results.title: Does a disclosed Ren service payment prove margin superiority over Foundation Source?
results.claim: Ren has higher profit margin than Foundation Source based on audited RCF payments and Charityvest expenses
results.conclusion: RCF has an audited $19,225,546 FY2024 payment to Ren; this does not establish either vendor's profitability or support a Ren-versus-Foundation-Source margin ranking.

frameworkUse.reason: no observed company-profit outcome to diagnose; measurement comparability problem only

results.counterargument: Either vendor could be more profitable after accounting for unrelated customers, labor, tech costs, acquisition accounting, and fee recognition; comparisons are not supported.
results.action: Obtain comparable payee-identified sponsor-to-vendor fee amounts and same-period recognized vendor revenue plus cost-to-serve records.
monitor: full service cost and margin per comparable product
results.reassessWhen: Reconciled audited vendor revenues and operating costs for comparable 2024–2026 service scopes are obtained.
